intent_en: To demonstrate that test-optional colleges attract more applicants than test-required colleges and that application volumes have increased over time.
previous_intent: To illustrate the increase in college applications over time, demonstrating that test-optional institutions attract more applicants than test-required institutions.
narration_support: First more students apply. Naturally, when universities make it easier to do so, whether by using the common application or removing requirements like test scores, more will.
chart_support: Line chart showing average applications from 1992 to 2010, where the test-optional trend line is consistently higher and rises more steeply than the test-required trend line.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly links removing requirements (like test scores) to more students applying. The chart visualizes this by showing application counts over time, with test-optional schools having significantly higher application numbers than test-required schools.
